newsitem.title: USA: New figures show deficit hitting new low.
newsitem.headline: New figures show deficit hitting new low.

text.p: The Congressional Budget Office estimates the deficit for the fiscal year ended September 30 will be lower than earlier thought, dropping to $109 billion, an internal memo showed Wednesday.
"We expect ... fiscal year 1996 to close with a deficit of $109 billion," said the memo from the non-partisan CBO.
In the memo, marked "not for public release," the CBO said its latest estimate could be off by $2 billion either way.
"The deficit for FY 1996 should be within the range of $107 billion to $111 billion," said the memo, made available to Reuters by a source.
The memo noted that the latest estimate is $7 billion lower than the CBO August estimate of $116 billion. And it is far lower than the May estimate of a $144 billion deficit.
The change is more good news for the Clinton administration, which has lowered the deficit four years in a row. The deficit is the lowest since 1981, when it was $79 billion.
